assessment.summary: Autonomous weapons are being fielded faster than the law governing them is being written; large General Assembly majorities back new rules, but several states with the most capable systems vote against them, leaving an arms race under no binding constraint as the most likely path.
assessment.timeframe: Ongoing, with a diplomatic deadline in view: the UN and the ICRC set 2026 as the target for a legally binding instrument, and the seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, in Geneva in November 2026, is described as the clearest path available for States to act.

claims.text: In a renewed joint appeal on 25 August 2026, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said: "We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines." The appeal renews a 2023 joint call for States to negotiate a legally binding agreement by 2026 and points to the seventh Review Conference of the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, in Geneva in November 2026, as the clearest path available.

On 1 December 2025 the General Assembly adopted its resolution on lethal autonomous weapons systems (A/C.1/80/L.41) by a recorded vote of 164 in favour to 6 against (Belarus, Burundi, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Israel, Russian Federation, United States), with 7 abstentions.

On 2 December 2024 the General Assembly adopted its resolution on lethal autonomous weapons systems (A/C.1/79/L.77) by a recorded vote of 166 in favour to 3 against (Belarus, Democratic People's Republic of Korea, Russian Federation), with 15 abstentions, expressing concern about the risk of an emerging arms race, exacerbation of existing conflicts, humanitarian crises and miscalculations, lowering the threshold for an escalation of conflicts and proliferation, including to unauthorized recipients such as non-State actors.

On 14 May 2025 the UN Secretary-General called lethal autonomous weapon systems "politically unacceptable" and "morally repugnant", said that machines with the power and discretion to take human lives without human control should be prohibited by international law, and urged Member States to agree clear regulations and prohibitions by 2026.

description: Lethal autonomous weapons systems are weapons that select and engage targets without meaningful human control over the decision to kill. No binding international instrument governs them. The UN General Assembly has adopted successive resolutions on the subject — 166 to 3 in December 2024, 164 to 6 in December 2025 — but several states with the most advanced programmes are among those voting against, and negotiations remain confined to an expert group under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons. The Secretary-General and the President of the International Committee of the Red Cross have jointly urged states to adopt rules by 2026, warning in August 2026 that the world is dangerously close to crossing a moral red line in the autonomous targeting of humans by machines. The risk here is less a single catastrophe than an unconstrained arms race that lowers the threshold for using force, compresses escalation below human reaction times, and proliferates to unauthorized recipients including non-State actors.
name: Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
